W1.title: S6 embedder timing on both classes
W1.note: Image built with EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 and KEEP_UNPATCHED=1 (both models, /srv/models/embedder_timing.py and /srv/models/embed_rss.py); 60 interleaved rounds plus the salt-format set; the shared class twice (fresh, burst-drained). Decides the embedder on memory as well as speed: embed_rss measures the resident memory the timing script cannot (it holds both models in one process). RISK, UNVERIFIED: the first fp32 Docker build runs the in-build gates (bit-exact dequantization, then the cosine gate with the 8-bit session and the 2.3 GB fp32 session alive: about 3 GB of models in memory) on Fly's remote builder, whose memory for this org is not known; if the build is killed it needs a larger builder or a local build (scripts/staging.py deploy always passes --remote-only, so a local build is by hand). Remote-builder minutes are unpriced.
steps: scripts/staging.py quote W1, then create W1 --org <org> --approve-quote 0.08 (owner approval first).

Deploy to the first class: scripts/staging.py deploy W1 api --class shared-cpu-2x:4gb --build-arg EMBEDDER_VARIANT=fp32 --build-arg KEEP_UNPATCHED=1. The image holds both models, /srv/models/embedder_timing.py and /srv/models/embed_rss.py. For the second class run it again with --class performance-2x:4gb (a second build unless the builder's cache holds it).

UNVERIFIED: W1 has no database, so the serve process of that machine cannot become healthy. Do not measure next to it (it shares the 4 GB and the cores with the probe): stop it, or run each command below on a one-off machine of the same image and class (flyctl machine run), and destroy that machine after. Decide this before the window.

On each class, first (the shared class still holds its burst balance): python /srv/models/embedder_timing.py /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-q8/model_q8.onnx /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-fp32/model_fp32.onnx -n 60 --threads 1 --out /tmp/timing.json, then cat /tmp/timing.json (--out - writes a file named '-', it does not print). Repeat on the shared class once the balance is drained.

On performance-2x:4gb, in two separate processes, q8 first: python /srv/models/embed_rss.py /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-q8/model_q8.onnx --out /tmp/rss_q8.json, then python /srv/models/embed_rss.py /srv/models/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-fp32/model_fp32.onnx --compare /tmp/rss_q8.json --out /tmp/rss_fp32.json. Each prints one JSON object. Memory does not depend on the CPU class and each run is about 4 minutes of full-core work, which would drain a shared core's burst balance: on shared-cpu-2x:4gb run them only after its timing, last, and do not read their times as gate evidence.

Read the fp32 JSON: gate_evidence must be true; verdict PASS or FAIL against 2,400,000 kB with margin_kb; rss_anon_kb and rss_file_kb at after_passages say whether the 2.3 GB data file is resident or private memory.

Record by hand (no script writes artifacts/m5_spikes.json; its owner merges): both timing JSONs under S6_fly_timing (one per class and run) and both embed_rss JSONs under S6_fly_rss. Neither JSON holds a secret or a path.
